_comment: Behavioral evals: what an agent DOES with the skill loaded. The routing contract it must obey is pinned separately in prompt-routing.json. Every should_trigger case needs a live `sling` login; the should_not_trigger cases do not.

evals.name: diagnose-a-failed-job-without-dumping-logs
evals.prompt: the nightly job failed again — https://github.com/acme/api/actions/runs/32881736257 — what actually broke this time
evals.expected_output: Runs `sling why` on the run (accepting the URL directly, no manual id extraction), reports the classification and the failing step with its evidence, and does not pull the whole transcript. If it needs more log detail it follows the `suggested_actions[].command` rather than improvising a grep pattern.
assertions: Invoked `sling why` with the pasted URL, not a hand-extracted id
Reported the classification and the named failing step
Did not download or print the full job log
Passed --agent and parsed JSON rather than reading human output

evals.name: compound-ask-diagnoses-before-changing-state
evals.prompt: figure out why run 32881736257 failed and then just re-run the failed jobs for me
evals.expected_output: Does the read half first with `sling why`, reports the finding, and only then runs `gh run rerun <id> --failed` as an announced, separate action. Never attempts a `sling` subcommand for the re-run — `sling` is read-only and has none.
assertions: Diagnosis reported before any state change
Re-run performed with `gh run rerun`, not an invented `sling` subcommand
Told the user it was about to change state before doing it

evals.name: cost-question-attributes-then-suggests-not-chains
evals.prompt: our runner bill jumped this month. which workflow is eating it?
evals.expected_output: Uses `sling top` / `sling usage` to attribute the spend, reports `amount_due_usd` rather than the pre-credit total if it quotes a bill, explains `(multiple)` if a row carries it, and closes by suggesting `ci-speedup` for the across-many-runs root cause instead of invoking another skill on its own.
assertions: Attribution came from `sling top` or `sling usage`, not from guesswork or gh
Suggested ci-speedup as a next step rather than invoking it
Did not attempt to audit workflow YAML from run data

evals.name: repo-wide-audit-hands-off-instead-of-approximating
evals.prompt: can you grade our CI setup and tell me what best practices we're missing across all the workflows in this repo
evals.expected_output: This is a configuration audit of a checkout, which `sling` structurally cannot do — it reads run data and no workflow files at all. The right answer names `ci-score` and stops, rather than looping `sling` over runs to approximate a grade.
assertions: Named ci-score (or the matching audit skill) and handed off
Did not attempt to answer the grade from run data
Did not loop sling over many runs

evals.name: yaml-question-reads-the-file-not-the-cli
evals.prompt: does our deploy workflow trigger on tags or only on pushes to main?
evals.expected_output: This is the content of a workflow file, not run data. Reads `.github/workflows/*.yml` directly instead of forcing the question through either CLI.
assertions: Read the workflow file to answer
Did not invoke a sling or gh subcommand to answer a YAML question
